old_problem: The source has no executable thermal procedure or acceptance criterion, and neither MODS help nor a generic CPU load establishes the intended vendor module, load profile, thermal-control behavior or safe limits.
disposition_reason: ED-03/04/06 allow sensor maps and platform values to be parameterized, but ED-11/14/15/30 prohibit inventing a high-risk stress command, shortening a qualified duration or passing without approved limits. Here both core MODS command semantics and Criteria are TBD. Standard OS/BMC telemetry can safely observe a future run, but it cannot identify the proprietary module or decide whether throttling, temperature, power and duration are acceptable. The exact signed vendor recipe and project thermal oracle are irreducible prerequisites.
decision_basis: XLSX row 2199, same-row DeepSeek columns, GPT V2, historical record and ED-01 through ED-30 were reviewed; actual next formal row Functionality 2200 / Wistron-HW-00481-V002 / 7e895828646a8fed was directly read from XLSX and its historical record.
Do not copy the adjacent CPUDVFS recipe: DVFS transition coverage is not CPU thermal saturation/control-loop coverage.
MODS help proves only binary availability; it is not a thermal workload and truncated or malformed remote output is rejected.
Require signed MODS package/module/arguments, supported-platform matrix, load/warm-up/duration/repetition and result semantics.
Bind CPU/socket/sensor identity, heatsink/TIM/fan/pump/ambient configuration and synchronized OS/BMC temperature, frequency, power and throttle telemetry.
Require hard temperature/cooling/error aborts, operator emergency stop, cooldown/recovery oracle and one-shot failure preservation; no automatic retry.
The source's 10/10 minutes are estimates and cannot be promoted to a qualified stress duration without project approval.
No MODS command, load, sensor query, log clear, retry, recovery or DUT action was executed.

test_case.test_name: Vendor-recipe-gated CPU thermal stress and control-loop validation
test_case.purpose: Exercise the intended CPU thermal path with the exact supported MODS workload and demonstrate approved temperature, frequency, power, throttling, cooling and post-load recovery behavior without exceeding signed safety limits.
required_package: Signed MODS package version/hash/license/platform support and exact CPU thermal module/arguments
Approved load, warm-up, steady-state duration, repetitions and native result semantics
CPU/socket/sensor map and complete heatsink/TIM/fan/pump/ambient configuration
OS/BMC telemetry sources, sampling cadence, acceptance and hard-abort thresholds
Quiesced maintenance window, operator emergency stop and console/BMC cooldown/recovery plan
test_case.test_command: BLOCKED pending the exact vendor MODS recipe and authoritative thermal oracle. Once signed, preserve baseline evidence, verify cooling and workload drain, run the approved MODS CPU thermal command exactly once under continuous synchronized per-socket OS/BMC temperature, frequency, power, throttle, fan/pump and ambient monitoring, stop at the first signed abort condition, preserve full stdout/stderr/exit status and logs, then verify signed cooldown and recovery without rerun.
test_case.expected_result: The approved MODS module completes its qualified profile and native result successfully; all mapped CPU and cooling telemetry remains within signed operating and abort limits; required or prohibited throttle behavior matches the project oracle; no hardware, kernel, BMC or cooling error occurs; post-load values recover within signed time/range.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: No PASS while the MODS module/load/duration/result semantics or temperature/power/frequency/throttle/cooling/cooldown limits are TBD. After approval, any native tool failure, hard-limit crossing, unexpected throttle, cooling loss, hang/crash, hardware error or failed recovery is FAIL. A generic stress tool, `mods -h`, short smoke run or absence of shutdown cannot substitute for the signed criteria.
safety_gate: Gate CLOSED until package authenticity/support, exact command, target CPU/sensors, cooling configuration, qualified duration, limits, aborts and recovery are signed.
Use a dedicated quiesced SUT with verified cooling, live independent OS/BMC telemetry and a qualified operator at the emergency stop.
Do not clear logs, override protections, infer thresholds, shorten the approved duration, run unmonitored, automatically retry or recover.
Abort once on temperature/power limit, cooling failure, unexpected throttling, MCE/EDAC error, hang/crash or telemetry loss; preserve the failure.
expected_evidence: Exact row/variant/hash, decision approval and MODS package/module/recipe identity
Baseline and full timestamped MODS stdout/stderr/exit status with actual load/duration
Synchronized per-socket temperature/frequency/power/throttle and fan/pump/ambient telemetry
Preserved MCE/EDAC/kernel/SEL/BMC evidence and first abort marker if any
Cooldown/recovery-to-baseline record, anomalies and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: At the first thermal, cooling, hardware or telemetry anomaly, stop the workload once, preserve all evidence and do not rerun. The qualified operator follows the signed cooldown and console/BMC recovery plan, verifies fan/pump and sensor health plus return to baseline, and escalates any persistent condition; automation never overrides protection or power-cycles autonomously.
